entries.title: Isaiah 22:1
segments: The valley of vision; Jerusalem, as being surrounded by hills higher than itself, and also the place where God in a special manner revealed himself.  If, as is most natural, we assume that this prophecy was uttered in immediate connection with that which follows against Shebna,
, its date must be placed before Sennacherib's invasion.  See note to
.  It may refer not only to that invasion, but also to the one that followed in Manasseh's day,

. 
 
  Gone up to the house-tops; to make observation, as was customary in the case of sudden alarms.  The roofs of oriental cities are nearly flat. 
 
Special religious privileges lay men under corresponding obligations to holiness, and the abuse of them will be punished with exemplary severity.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:2
segments:
Thou that art full; that is, customarily. 
 
  Not slain with the sword--dead in battle; they perish from famine and pestilence accompanying the siege.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:3
segments: Bound; taken captive and bound.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:4
segments: Good men bitterly grieve over the calamities which befall God's people.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:5
segments: Crying to the mountains; the cry of distress resounding to the neighboring mountains.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:6
segments:
Elam; Persia. 
 
  Kir; the modern Georgia, lying between the Black and the Caspian seas.  These two countries are named as subject to the king of Assyria and furnishing troops for his service.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:7
segments: Shall be full of chariots--at the gate; this may have been in Sennacherib's day, or when the king of Assyria took Manasseh captive and carried him to Babylon.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:8
segments:
He discovered; literally, "he uncovered." 
 
  The covering of Judah; her defences. 
 
  Thou didst look; the king with his princes. 
 
  The house of the forest; "the house of the forest of Lebanon," built by Solomon,
, and used as an armory.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:9
segments:
Seen also; examined, for the purpose of repairing. 
 
  Gathered together the waters; to cut them off from the enemy.
The lower pool; lying in the valley of Hinnom, south-west of Zion.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:11
segments:
A ditch; rather, "a reservoir."  This was to shut off the water from the enemy. 
 
  The old pool; the upper pool of Gihon, lying west of the city, towards the head of the valley of Hinnom. 
 
  The maker thereof--him that fashioned it; that is, God, who of old ordained this calamity.

All outward means should be used in humble dependence upon God.  When forgetting him, we give to these our chief confidence, we dishonor his almighty power and supremacy, and he will make us feel that vain is the help of man.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:12
segments:
Baldness; the shaving of the hair as a sign of grief. 
 
vv 12-14. 
 
When God's judgments, instead of bringing men to repentance, become the occasion of their hardening themselves in sin, they are reprobate, and their destruction is at hand.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:13
segments: Let us eat and drink; for to-morrow we shall die; the words of the besieged, hardening themselves in carnal mirth against the approaching calamity.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:14
segments: Purged from you; expiated and forgiven.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:15
segments: Shebna; in the account of Sennacherib's invasion, we find Shebna already superseded by Eliakim, as "over the house."

, etc.  Hence this prophecy must have been uttered before that invasion. 
 
  Over the house; over the king's household.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:16
segments:
What hast thou--whom hast thou; what right--what man of thy kindred?  The prophet reminds Shebna that he has no right to a sepulchre at Jerusalem, and that his vanity shall be punished by disgrace and exile.  The ancients expended large sums upon their supulchres, which were generally hewn out of rocks. 
 
vv 16-19. 
 
All ostentation is offensive to God, but that which respects the resting place of our ashes is in a peculiar degree foolish and wicked. They who indulge themselves in such vanity, may expect an ignominious instead of an honorable end.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:18
segments: The shame of thy lord's house; or, "thou shame of thy lord's house.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:20
segments:
vv 20-23. 
 
God will, in his own time and way, advance his humble and faithful servants to places of trust and honor, so far as he shall see it to be for their own welfare and that of his people.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:21
segments: Thy robe; the robe of office.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:22
segments:
Key; here used as a symbol of authority. 
 
  Shall open--none shall shut; shall have uncontrolled power.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:23
segments:
Fasten him--in a sure place; firmly fix him in his station. 
 
  A glorious throne; a seat where all the members of his father's family may find honorable repose.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:24
segments:
They shall hang upon him; he shall support them, as a nail or pin supports the vessel hung upon it. 
 
  The off-spring and the issue; the noble and the base of his family, who are compared, in the remainder of the verse, to vessels of different sorts and sizes. 
 
When a righteous man is prospered and honored he becomes a stay and support, not only to the good generally, but in a special sense to those of his own household.

entries.title: Isaiah 22:25
segments: The nail that is fastened; that is, Shebna, who is now as a nail fastened.
